subject: World-model wipe fix: REJECTED as a measured regression.
change: cell-8 monkeypatch of ToolAgent._update_summarized_knowledge_from_step_summary: keep action_model across a level change, wipe nothing on game_over. Everything else byte-identical to the D-undo control.
verdict: REJECT. Do not ship, do not add to the rotation.
why_this_is_not_noise: BOTH pass-matched rows agree in sign (-5 and -9). The within-config null was 10 up / 2 down in the SAME direction; this arm reverses it to 2 up / 14 down.
The arm's WORSE pass (27) and BETTER pass (28) both fall below the control's WORSE pass (33).
The gap of -21 pooled levels is more than 2x the control's own internal pass spread of 10.
The single-point trap is checked: the ex-ft09 mean moves the same way (-1.757), so this is not one game carrying the result.
rule_applied: CLAUDE.md rule 15(c): NEVER ship a MEASURED REGRESSION. This is the one hard exclusion. Note the literal rule-15 reject threshold ('level total <= 18') is written for a SINGLE-pass run; on a 2-pass run the comparable figure is <= 36 and this arm is 55, so the reject rests on the paired split and the sign agreement across both passes, not on the level total.
what_it_teaches: The wipe was doing useful work. Carrying action_model and the world model across a level transition made the agent WORSE, which is the opposite of the mechanism argument. Most plausible reading: a stale model from level N actively misleads on level N+1, and the blanket wipe was cheap insurance against that. This is the 8th overlay-class arm on this harness and the 8th not to win.
still_true_and_still_free: The ACTION7 batch-rejection repair in the same bundle is unaffected and stays. The animation() prompt repair was NOT in this arm.
